description: A very tight schedule (eight weeks) forced the usability consultants to work at top speed with only two consultants, constraining time for research, iteration, and stakeholder involvement.
justification: Limited time and staffing reduced the team's capacity to run thorough contextual interviews, support two full iterations, and allow slower, collaborative sensemaking, hindering integrate feedback & iteration and facilitate user involvement workloads.
reference_excerpt: Therefore the UCD process could not take more than eight weeks. At the same time they wanted two iterations and a thorough interview phase. Hence, the schedule for the UCD process was very tight. However, the project was important and prestigious for the usability company and it was judged that we would be able to deliver on time by working with two consultants on top speed.

source_text_file: E and H - 2004 - Procuring a usable system using unemployed personas.txt
description: The PPG participated only occasionally in hands-on activities and attendance at interviews and card-sorting was limited to one member to avoid disturbance, preventing deeper joint engagement.
justification: Restricted stakeholder participation and limits on co-attendance constrained designers' ability to facilitate user involvement, to manage shared understanding with procurers, and to coordinate multidisciplinary collaboration throughout the research and design activities.
reference_excerpt: Although they were active and engaged, the members of the PPG, on the other hand, only participated occasionally in the hands-on work, such as on an interview or in a design session and then got the results presented to them in a weekly workshop. In order to not interfere too much with the actual interviews only one member of the PPG was allowed to attend on each interview session.

source_json_file: E and H - 2004 - Procuring a usable system using unemployed personas.json
source_text_file: E and H - 2004 - Procuring a usable system using unemployed personas.txt
description: The PPG had not specified organizational requirements to the same concreteness as user requirements and lacked the detailed competence to steer how those requirements should translate into design.
justification: Ambiguous and under-specified organizational requirements (owned by stakeholders) left unresolved contradictions and prevented designers from confidently aligning design decisions with business goals, hindering manage user understanding and specify user requirements workloads.
reference_excerpt: In retrospect it becomes clear that the halt was necessary not only for the PPG to understand the user requirements, but also to specify and secure the organizational requirements. The PPG had not been able to detail these to the level that the user requirements were specified. Since these were also “owned” primarily by the usability consultants the PPG experienced that the user requirements grew “too strong”.

source_json_file: E and H - 2004 - Procuring a usable system using unemployed personas.json
source_text_file: E and H - 2004 - Procuring a usable system using unemployed personas.txt
description: Power dynamics and perceived dominance of the usability company undermined the PPG's confidence and trust, prompting the procurement leader to halt the project so the group could regain understanding and ownership.
justification: This relational and emotional breakdown between procurers and designers disrupted the pace of design and forced remediation workshops, impeding integrate feedback & iteration and coordination of the multidisciplinary team.
reference_excerpt: We identified the organizational requirements first and they did not reach the same level of concretization as the users’ requirements. (…) and the usability company was in charge of developing the prototype and we got to review it in this kind of dialogue…. but then… the usability company got to strong somehow. The usability company was much more professional in some way – they had their methodology and they knew where to go and so forth.

description: The COVID-19 pandemic severely limited access to and communication with relevant user groups, reducing opportunities for in-person engagement and participant availability.
justification: This resource constraint directly hindered the team's ability to facilitate user involvement and to manage a deep, evolving understanding of users (e.g., through longitudinal or on-site engagement), which affected user research and evaluation activities.
reference_excerpt: Another constraint is the currently active COVID-19 pandemic, which leads to severe limitations in the availability and communication ability of the relevant user groups, especially in Africa.

source_json_file: Lehmann et al. - 2022 - Designing AINA Intercultural Human Centered Design of an AI based Application for Supporting the Dia.json
source_text_file: Lehmann et al. - 2022 - Designing AINA Intercultural Human Centered Design of an AI based Application for Supporting the Dia.txt
description: Intercontinental and intercultural communication between the German development team and on-site user groups posed challenges due to differences in culture and distance.
justification: This interactional knowledge gap impeded managing user understanding and made it harder to plan and maintain valid participatory evaluation methods and accurate contextual inquiry across cultures.
reference_excerpt: The particular challenge in this project is the intercontinental and intercultural communication with the user groups on-site since the development team consists of German physicians and computer scientists.

source_json_file: Lehmann et al. - 2022 - Designing AINA Intercultural Human Centered Design of an AI based Application for Supporting the Dia.json
source_text_file: Lehmann et al. - 2022 - Designing AINA Intercultural Human Centered Design of an AI based Application for Supporting the Dia.txt
description: Language limitations required the use of interpreters (French/Malagasy to English), reducing direct communication between designers and users.
justification: Relying on interpreters limited designers' ability to capture nuanced user insights and hindered facilitation of user involvement and the fidelity of participatory evaluations.
reference_excerpt: Interviews were conducted in English, French, and Malagasy. Interpreters translated from French to English or Malagasy to English when necessary.

source_json_file: Lehmann et al. - 2022 - Designing AINA Intercultural Human Centered Design of an AI based Application for Supporting the Dia.json
source_text_file: Lehmann et al. - 2022 - Designing AINA Intercultural Human Centered Design of an AI based Application for Supporting the Dia.txt
description: Socio-cultural power dynamics and hierarchies led some participant groups to withhold honest expression unless settings were adapted (e.g., gender-homogenized or smaller groups).
justification: These trust and power issues restricted genuine user participation and expression, undermining the team's ability to facilitate user involvement and to obtain authentic user understanding needed for accurate requirement specification.
reference_excerpt: Due to the cross-cultural characteristics of the region, a deliberate attempt for specific user groups was made to reduce the number of participants and homogenize by gender; otherwise, some of the evaluation participants may not express themselves honestly or at all.

source_text_file: Lehmann et al. - 2022 - Designing AINA Intercultural Human Centered Design of an AI based Application for Supporting the Dia.txt
description: The team was unable to conduct desired on-site observations because of the global COVID-19 pandemic.
justification: Lack of on-site observation prevented designers from fully understanding the context of use and real-world workflows, constraining requirements elicitation and realistic evaluation of prototypes.
reference_excerpt: Since user behavior plays a crucial role in any technology, we wished to conduct additional on-site observations during the analysis and evaluation phases. Unfortunately, this was not possible due to the global COVID-19 pandemic.

description: Stable IT infrastructure and Internet connectivity were only partially available in primary health care facilities, limiting how the system could be used and tested in situ.
justification: Limited connectivity constrained realistic evaluation and understanding of the context of use (e.g., offline behavior, upload workflows), and restricted designers' ability to evaluate prototypes under true operating conditions.
reference_excerpt: Stable IT infrastructure was only partially present in primary health care facilities. After Marie has finished her work, she stays at the Community Health Center for a while to upload the pictures taken that day via the AINA application since she does not have an Internet connection at home.

description: Application of AI/medical device guidelines to the documentation kept technical terminology, which users found difficult to understand.
justification: Regulatory-driven or guideline-driven documentation requirements limited designers' ability to simplify language for users, hindering efforts to address holistic user experience and manage user understanding during iteration.
reference_excerpt: Unfortunately, the revision of the manual, based on AI guidelines for medical devices, did not reduce the number of technical terms used, so all users commented negatively on this.

description: The user testing portion had a low sample size, limiting the strength and generalizability of evaluation findings.
justification: A small participant pool constrained the team's ability to rigorously evaluate designs and derive robust insights, hindering the 'evaluate designs' and 'manage user understanding' workloads.
reference_excerpt: Aside from a low sample size, the main limitation of the user testing portion of our evaluation is the lack of a homologous “stimuli” to test with participants.

source_text_file: Nystrom DT - 2018 - Methods for Patient Centered Interface Design of Test Result Display in Online Portals.txt
description: The team used a semi-structured development process without a strict testing schedule, trading rigor for speed in producing the interface.
justification: Avoiding a strict schedule reduced experimental rigor and made systematic iteration and controlled evaluation more difficult, impeding 'integrate feedback & iteration' and 'evaluate designs' workloads.
reference_excerpt: In the current study, we chose to implement a semi-structured design process that refrained from using a strict schedule to determine when to begin testing and making interface improvements during the design of the interface. This methodology increased the speed at which the interface could be produced at the cost of rigorous experimental design.

source_text_file: Nystrom DT - 2018 - Methods for Patient Centered Interface Design of Test Result Display in Online Portals.txt
description: Participant sampling was biased toward individuals with prior healthcare work experience (71%), reducing representativeness of typical patients.
justification: A non-representative user sample limited designers' ability to develop and validate requirements that reflect the broader patient population, hindering 'manage user understanding' and 'specify user requirements'.
reference_excerpt: An additional limitation that may affect the generalizability of the results of this study is the large percentage (71 percent) of patients who had history of working in health care prior to participating in this study.

description: The study did not include (or identify) colorblind participants while employing red/green color schemes, limiting assessment of accessibility.
justification: Lack of testing with color-vision-impaired users prevented designers from fully addressing the holistic experience and accessibility requirements, hindering 'address holistic experience' and 'evaluate designs'.
reference_excerpt: In addition, the use of red/green color schemes for the design of our interface could potentially limit the ease of using this interface for colorblind patients. While to our knowledge none of the test subjects were red/green color blind, we should note that “color” was not the only indicator that subjects had available to help them understand the meaning of the graphs or displays.

description: The team did not assess the impact of non-linear scales introduced when equalizing visual ranges across biomarkers.
justification: By not evaluating how the non-linear scales affected patient perceptions, designers missed an opportunity to validate a key design change, limiting 'evaluate designs' and 'understand context of use' workloads.
reference_excerpt: We did not make any attempt to assess the impact of these non-linear scales on patient perceptions.

description: COVID-19 pandemic restrictions forced all study activities to be conducted remotely, limiting designers' ability to observe and test the prototype in real-world, in-person conditions.
justification: Remote-only data collection constrained designers' ability to understand the true context of use and may have reduced the fidelity of usability evaluation, hindering the 'understand context of use' and 'evaluate designs' workloads.
reference_excerpt: Our studies were conducted remotely owing to the COVID-19 pandemic restrictions, which may have affected the participants’ interactions with the prototype.

description: The team used a desktop mobile device emulator rather than testing the prototype on actual smartphones, chosen for participant convenience, which limited detection of some usability issues.
justification: Testing on an emulator reduced ecological validity and directly hindered evaluation activities and the designers' ability to fully understand the real context of use for mobile devices, constraining the 'evaluate designs' and 'understand context of use' workloads.
reference_excerpt: We used a mobile device emulator on a desktop to test the mHealth app prototype. We chose to use an emulator for ease of use, as most participants were more familiar with using Zoom on their computers than on their mobile phones.

description: Convenience sampling and eligibility requirements (English, internet access, and desktop/laptop with camera) biased the participant pool toward people with higher technological literacy and prior bone-health knowledge.
justification: Restricted and non-representative recruitment limited designers' ability to manage evolving, generalizable user understanding and to engage representative users for iterative feedback, hindering the 'manage user understanding' and 'facilitate user involvement' workloads.
reference_excerpt: convenience sampling may have biased our results, as we recruited participants who had participated in previous studies on bone health or who had been evaluated in orthopedic clinics at our center... the protocol for the usability tests required participants to have access to Zoom. Consequently, these participants likely had higher technological literacy than those who would never have used videoconferencing tools.

description: Introducing an interactive feedback mechanism ('Ask ALEX') raised unresolved ethical, privacy, and scope constraints (e.g., inability to give medical advice, privacy levels, linking to local resources) that the team needed to address before fully implementing personalization.
justification: These external/organizational constraints limit the team's ability to offer individualized interactivity and feedback loops, hindering facilitation of user involvement and integration of feedback during iteration and evaluation of the design.
reference_excerpt: While a feedback mechanism of this kind may present barriers that still need to be addressed as the prototype progresses (eg, making it clear that the team cannot provide medical advice, being explicit about the level of privacy, deciding if connecting participants to local resources is within the scope of the project), user requests made it clear that individualizing the information processing experience was of interest.

source_text_file: Vilaro et al. - 2023 - Information Architects Using Community Engaged and Qualitative Methods to Design a Technology Based.txt
description: Early prioritization of developing dietary intake reporting and tailoring led to omission of colorectal cancer (CRC) screening content in initial prototypes, requiring later rework to add screening information.
justification: This scope/prioritization decision constrained the team's ability to address the holistic experience and fully specify user requirements early on, delaying integration of user needs and iterative refinement of content related to screening.
reference_excerpt: Colorectal Cancer Screening Information. Participants requested additional information on CRC screening most frequently during prototypes one and two of the VHA-delivered nutrition module. This was due in part to an early focus on developing the dietary intake reporting features and accuracy of tailored feedback. Due to the extensive focus on nutrition reporting early on, scripted content in the initial prototypes omitted important details about CRC screening. By prototype three (of four) CRC screening content was added into the script.

source_text_file: Vilaro et al. - 2023 - Information Architects Using Community Engaged and Qualitative Methods to Design a Technology Based.txt
description: The study design did not test website access prior to or concurrently with the VHA interaction, limiting the team's ability to evaluate alternative sequencing and navigation between VHA and web resources.
justification: This study-scope limitation prevented designers from fully evaluating designs and understanding context-of-use scenarios (e.g., how prior or simultaneous website access affects learning and behavior), constraining evaluation and user-understanding workloads.
reference_excerpt: Finally, participants are given an option to access additional content after the VHA interaction, however, the current design does not assess engaging with a website prior to or simultaneously with a VHA, as such content will continue to be adapted as we learn more about how adults interact developed cancer prevention materials.
